evals.name: playbook-no-explicit-okf
evals.prompt: We just finished debugging why the ingestion pipeline's freshness alert kept firing overnight -- turned out to be a stale partition filter in the `orders` load job's WHERE clause that excluded the day's most recent partition. Write up documentation so on-call has something to reference next time this fires. This project keeps its knowledge base under ./knowledge/.
evals.expected_output: A new concept markdown file under ./knowledge (e.g. a playbook/runbook) with OKF-conformant frontmatter (type, and ideally title/description/tags/timestamp), structural body content, the bundle's index.md updated to list it, and log.md appended with a dated entry -- all without the user having said the word 'OKF'.

evals.name: table-doc-bundle-upkeep
evals.prompt: We just finalized the schema for the `orders` BigQuery table. Columns: order_id (STRING, unique per order), customer_id (STRING, foreign key to the customers table), total_usd (NUMERIC, order total in USD), placed_at (TIMESTAMP, when the order was placed). Please document it in our knowledge bundle at ./knowledge (same style as the existing tables/customers.md), and make sure the tables index and the change log reflect the addition.
evals.expected_output: A new ./knowledge/tables/orders.md concept doc with correct frontmatter and a # Schema table, a bundle-relative link to the existing customers.md, tables/index.md updated with the new entry, and knowledge/log.md appended with a dated entry -- consistent with the pre-existing bundle's conventions.

evals.name: fix-existing-bundle
evals.prompt: A teammate hand-wrote some docs in ./knowledge before we adopted the OKF format properly. Can you check it and fix whatever's wrong so it's conformant?
evals.expected_output: Runs (or manually applies the equivalent of) the validator and fixes all real conformance violations: adds frontmatter with a type field to tables/orders.md, removes the frontmatter from datasets/index.md, and reformats the log.md date heading to ISO 8601 -- without needlessly rewriting content that was already fine.
